sections.name: intro
sections.note: the pad alone: one chord every two bars

sections.name: signal
sections.note: the whistle over all of it, twice

sections.name: rally
sections.note: hard cut: a crowd, a drone, metal

sections.name: build
sections.note: the kit comes back tight; the crowd recedes

sections.name: strip
sections.note: the wall is taken down; the signal, slower

sections.name: fade
sections.note: snare and hats go; a sparse kick and the bass do not let up

motifs.name: tread
motifs.note: the riff's first bar: the root in eighths, leaning on one and three, a breath after the third note, one fifth popped on four

motifs.name: turn
motifs.note: its answer: half a bar of root, then under it -- the seventh, the fifth -- and back by way of the flat second

motifs.name: turn_hi
motifs.note: the fourth bar: a hole where the second note was, the same flat second home

motifs.name: riff
motifs.note: four bars. Everything else stands on this

motifs.name: alarm
motifs.note: the whistle: two bars, three-three-two, a fourth up and back, then a third. A signal, not a tune

motifs.name: alarm_out
motifs.note: its first two notes, then the one note that fits nothing under it, held

motifs.name: signal
motifs.note: eight bars: the signal three times and its way out

motifs.name: alarm_far
motifs.note: the signal at half speed: what is left after the wall

motifs.name: ring
motifs.note: the guitars: the riff's eighths with holes punched in them, and its flat second (`ms match`: the reference's wall has five hits a second)

motifs.name: mute
motifs.note: one note, eight times, leaning on one and three: the guitar before it is a wall

motifs.name: mute_hi
motifs.note: one note, eight times, leaning on one and three: the guitar before it is a wall

motifs.name: ground
motifs.note: the pad's floor: the two bass notes

motifs.name: watch
motifs.note: the pad's top: with the ground, a fifth, a sixth, a sixth, a fifth

motifs.name: anvil
motifs.note: the clank: three against four, and a stumble. One pitch; metal does not follow the chords

ops.note: `ms match --stems`: the reference's bass sits out the first half of the build
`ms match`: 15 dB brighter than the reference's bass above 1 kHz
`ms match`: the reference has 45% of its energy under 80 Hz
two sixteenths of snare before the downbeat
a snare stumble at the end of the fourth bar
a snare stumble at the end of the fourth bar
`ms match --stems`: in the reference's last section the top of the kit is gone and its backbeat band is 14 dB down; what holds is a sparse kick
the kit carries the top of the mix now, and the reference's top is 8 dB darker
`ms match --stems`: the reference's kit is level with its bass; this one was 11 dB under
struck twice, far off, under the crowd
locked to the grid from here to the end
through a bad microphone
the signal, half speed, twice
a sine pushed until it has an edge
there the moment the band is cut; swells for six bars; takes the build to go away
until no one pitch can be picked out
`ms hear`: one recording thirty-two times in a row
a fifth above: between them, power chords
the octave, in the middle and further back
a breathy flute, fluttering, as the band goes
